title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a Nepali (really? no way! wow! damn!), use the little words that give speech its tone, add tag questions, use echo words, ask people to repeat or explain a word, and mix in English the way Nepalis do.
intro:
You can be grammatically perfect and still sound like a textbook. What makes Nepali sound *Nepali* is the small stuff: the **हगि?** at the end of a sentence, the **त** and **पो** that change its tone, the **ला!** and **हत्तेरी!** of surprise and annoyance, the **चिया-सिया** echo words, and the English words dropped into almost every sentence.

This unit collects them. The grammar is three sets of little words: **tag questions** (है, होइन, हगि, नि, र, कि), **emphatic particles** (त, नै, पो, न and the -ऐ ending) and **echo words** (चिया-सिया 'tea and stuff'). You'll also learn how to keep a conversation going when you don't understand: asking someone to repeat, to slow down, or to explain a word.

vocab.note: ला, तिमी यहाँ! "Whoa, you're here!". ला ला! can also mean "oh dear".
गजब भयो! "that's amazing!" — also ironic: "well, that's great (not)".
छक्क पर्नु "to be amazed": म त छक्क परेँ "I was stunned".
ठट्टा गर्नु "to joke". Also मजाक.
म सिरियस छु "I'm serious".
Contrast or emphasis: म त जान्छु "I, for one, am going". After a command: हेर त "just look".
आज नै "today itself", यही नै "this very one".

vocab.en: (particle) actually, contrary to what you thought
vocab.note: यो पो! "no, THIS one!"; ऊ त डाक्टर पो रहेछ "turns out he's actually a doctor".

vocab.en: (particle) softens a request: go on, do
vocab.note: बस न "do sit down"; भन न "go on, tell me".
Mild and very common. Also हत्तेरिका.
Also disapproval: छिः, कस्तो लाज! "ugh, how shameful!".
Casual Kathmandu speech, with friends. Less casual: होइन? / हैन?

vocab.en: well, to be fair; it's true that
vocab.note: Concedes a point before a "but": हुन त हो, तर… "that's true, but…".
As common as ठीक छ among young people.
X को अर्थ के हो? "what does X mean?" In speech, X भनेको के हो? is even more common.
Polite request: दोहोर्‍याइदिनुहोस् "please repeat (for me)".

vocab.en: arrangement, a fix (often a quiet one)
vocab.note: सेटिङ मिलाउनु "to arrange things, pull strings". Can hint at something under the table.
लेट भयो "I'm/it's late"; लेट गर्नु "to be late". Native: ढिलो.
खास केही छैन "nothing much"; खास गरी "especially".
A pair word built on गफ "chat": गफगाफ गर्नु "to hang out and chat".
Pair word: लुगा + फाटो.
Pair word: भाँडा + कुँडा.

phrases.en: Could you say that once more?
Could you give me an example?
Let's have some tea or something.

grammar.title: Tag questions: है, होइन, हगि, नि, र, कि
grammar.body:
Nepali hangs little words on the end of sentences to ask for agreement, soften, or show doubt. Each has its own job:

**है** — 'OK? / isn't it?' Seeks agreement or softens a request: राम्रो छ, **है**? 'nice, isn't it?'; भोलि आऊ **है** 'come tomorrow, OK?'. Very common in goodbyes: जाऊँ **है**.

**होइन? / हैन?** — 'right? isn't that so?' after a statement you expect to be true: तिमी पनि आउँछौ, **होइन**? 'you're coming too, aren't you?'

**हगि?** — the casual Kathmandu 'right?', used among friends: दामी छ, **हगि**? Don't use it with your boss.

**नि** — 'you know; then; what about…?' It does several things: reminds (म भनेँ **नि** 'I told you, didn't I'), asks back (तिमी **नि**? 'and you?'), and pushes a question (कहाँ गयो **नि**? 'so where did it go, then?').

**र** — at the end of a question, adds surprise or doubt: ऊ आयो **र**? 'did he actually come?'; **हो र**? 'really?'. In a rhetorical question it means 'of course not': मलाई के थाहा **र**? 'how would I know?'

**कि** — at the end, a tentative 'or…?, maybe?': तिमी पनि आउँछौ **कि**? 'are you coming too, perhaps?' It makes invitations and requests gentler (मिलाइदिनुहुन्छ **कि**? in unit 35).

They stack: भोलि आउँछौ, **होइन त**? · ठीक छ **नि त**!

examples.en: You're coming on Saturday too, aren't you?
I told you before, didn't I.
Did he really quit his job?
Fancy a cup of tea, maybe?

grammar.title: Little words with big effects: त, नै, पो, न, -ऐ
grammar.body:
These particles carry the *tone* of spoken Nepali. They're hard to translate one-to-one, but learners who use them sound instantly more natural.

**त** — contrast or emphasis on the word before it: **म त** जान्छु 'well, *I'm* going (whatever you do)'; यो **त** राम्रो छ 'this one's good, though'. After a command it means 'just, go on': हेर **त**! 'just look!'; भन **त** 'go on, say it'.

**नै** — 'exactly, the very, itself': आज **नै** 'today itself, this very day'; यही **नै** हो 'this is the one'; तपाईं **नै** भन्नुहोस् 'you tell me (you decide)'. With negatives: कोही **नै** आएन 'nobody at all came'.

**पो** — contrary to expectation, 'actually, oh but': ऊ त नेपाली **पो** रहेछ 'turns out he's actually Nepali'; त्यो होइन, यो **पो**! 'not that one — *this* one!'; म **पो** जान्छु 'no, *I'll* go'. It pairs naturally with रहेछ (surprise).

**न** — softens and encourages, after commands and requests: बस **न** 'do sit down'; भन **न** 'go on, tell me'; मिलाइदिनुहोस् **न** 'please sort it out'. Without न, a bare command can sound abrupt.

**-ऐ** — an emphatic ending glued onto words: आज → **आजै** 'this very day', अहिले → **अहिल्यै** 'right now', यहाँ → **यहीँ** 'right here', घरमा → **घरमै** 'at home itself', थाहा → **थाहै** छैन 'had no idea at all'.

**Fast speech.** In Kathmandu, the -एको ending is often squeezed to **-या**: के **गर्या**? (= गरेको) 'what are you doing?', के **भन्या**? (= भनेको) 'what did you say?'. You'll hear it constantly; the full form is always correct.

examples.native: म त अहिल्यै जान्छु, तिमीहरू बस।
examples.roman: ma ta ahilyai jānchhu, timiharu basa.
examples.en: Well, I'm off right now — you lot stay.

examples.native: यो रेस्टुरेन्ट त राम्रो पो रहेछ!
examples.roman: yo resṭurenṭ ta rāmro po rahechha!
examples.en: Oh, this restaurant is actually good!
Nobody at all came to the party.

examples.native: एकछिन बस न, किन हतार गरेको?
examples.roman: ekchhin basa na, kina hatār gareko?
examples.en: Sit down a minute — what's the hurry?
I had no idea at all!

grammar.title: Echo words and pair words
grammar.body:
Nepali loves **echo words**: you repeat a noun with its first sound replaced by **स-**, and the meaning becomes 'X and stuff like that, X or something':

**चिया-सिया** 'tea and things' · **काम-साम** 'work and all that' · **किताब-सिताब** 'books and stuff' · **फोन-सोन** 'a call or anything' · **पार्टी-सार्टी** 'a party or something'.

It makes a sentence casual and vague in a friendly way: चिया-सिया खाऔँ न 'let's have tea or something'. Echo words belong to relaxed talk among friends and family, not formal speech. Use the common ones you hear rather than inventing new ones.

Nepali also has fixed **pair words**, two words (or a word and a rhyming partner) that together mean 'X and the like': **गफगाफ** 'chit-chat', **लुगाफाटो** 'clothes and things', **भाँडाकुँडा** 'pots and pans', **हल्लाखल्ला** 'noise and commotion', **दाजुभाइ** 'brothers' (unit 3). These are normal words, fine in any register.

A related habit is **doubling** for variety or distribution (unit 8): के-के किन्यौ? 'what (all) did you buy?', को-को आए? 'who (all) came?', साना-साना 'little ones'.

examples.en: Come over this evening, we'll have tea or something.
We were chatting last night and suddenly it was one o'clock.

dialogue.title: Did you hear?
dialogue.setting: Emma, who is learning Nepali, meets her friend Sabin at a tea shop in Patan.

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: ए एम्मा! कति लेट गरेको? म आधा घण्टादेखि यहीँ छु नि।
lines.roman: e Emmā! kati leṭ gareko? ma ādhā ghanṭādekhi yahiṃ chhu ni.
lines.en: Hey, Emma! Why so late? I've been sitting here for half an hour.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: सरी सरी, जाममा परेँ। अनि, के छ खबर?
lines.roman: sari sari, jāmmā pareṃ. ani, ke chha khabar?
lines.en: Sorry, sorry, I got stuck in traffic. So, what's new?

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: खास केही छैन। अनि थाहा छ? हाम्रो अफिसको सागर छ नि, उसको त बिहे पो भएछ!
lines.roman: khās kehi chhaina. ani thāhā chha? hāmro aphisko Sāgar chha ni, usko ta bihe po bhaechha!
lines.en: Nothing much. But guess what? You know Sagar from my office — turns out he's got married!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: साँच्चै भनेको? गएको हप्ता त म सिंगल छु भन्दै थियो!
lines.roman: sāṃchchai bhaneko? gaeko haptā ta ma siṅgal chhu bhandai thiyo!
lines.en: Seriously? Last week he was going around saying he was single!

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: त्यही त! गफगाफ गर्दा केही भनेन, एक्कासि फेसबुकमा फोटो!
lines.roman: tyahi ta! gaphgāph gardā kehi bhanena, ekkāsi phesbukmā phoṭo!
lines.en: Exactly! Didn't say a word when we were chatting, then suddenly — photos on Facebook!

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.en: Ekkāsi means the same as achānak — "suddenly".

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: ए, बुझेँ। अलि बिस्तारै बोल न, तिमी त एकदम छिटो बोल्छौ, हगि।
lines.roman: e, bujheṃ. ali bistārai bola na, timi ta ekdam chhiṭo bolchhau, hagi.
lines.en: Ah, got it. Slow down a bit — you talk really fast, you know.

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: हाहा, सरी। अनि बिहे पनि लभ म्यारेज पो रहेछ, केटी जापानकी रे।
lines.roman: hāhā, sari. ani bihe pani labh myārej po rahechha, keṭi Jāpānki re.
lines.en: Haha, sorry. And get this, it was a love marriage — the girl's from Japan, apparently.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: बाबै! गजब भयो त। हामीलाई पार्टी-सार्टी दिन्छ कि?
lines.roman: bābai! gajab bhayo ta. hāmilāi pārṭi-sārṭi dinchha ki?
lines.en: Wow! That's amazing. Do you think he'll throw us a party or something?

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: ला! "पार्टी-सार्टी" पनि भन्न थाल्यौ? तिमी त नेपाली नै भइसक्यौ!
lines.roman: lā! "pārṭi-sārṭi" pani bhanna thālyau? timi ta nepāli nai bhaisakyau!
lines.en: Whoa! You're even saying 'party-sharty' now? You've turned Nepali!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: हुन त हो, तर उच्चारण अझै गाह्रो छ।
lines.roman: hun ta ho, tara uchchāran ajhai gāhro chha.
lines.en: Well, maybe, but the pronunciation is still hard.

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: चिन्ता नगर, एकदम राम्रो छ। लौ, चिया-सिया खाऔँ।
lines.roman: chintā nagara, ekdam rāmro chha. lau, chiyā-siyā khāauṃ.
lines.en: Don't worry, it's really good. Come on, let's have some tea.

culture:
Nepali conversation is full of **feedback noises**: listeners keep saying **अँ**, **हो**, **हो र?**, **ओहो!**, **अनि?** 'and then?' to show they're following. Staying silent can seem cold. The polite way to say 'pardon?' is **हजुर?** — a word that also answers when someone calls your name and means 'yes' to elders. With friends, just **के?** or **के भन्या?**

**English is everywhere.** Educated Kathmandu speech mixes in English words constantly — *actually, basically, seriously, sorry, OK, late, free, tension, setting* — always with Nepali grammar around them: लेट **भयो**, फ्री **छौ**?, टेन्सन **नलेऊ**, सेटिङ **मिलाउँछु**. Don't be shy about doing the same; a fully Sanskritised Nepali sentence can sound more foreign than one with *OK* in it. With older people and in villages, use the Nepali words.

When you don't understand, Nepalis are usually delighted to explain: **X भनेको के हो?** 'what does X mean?' or **यसलाई नेपालीमा के भन्छन्?** 'what do you call this in Nepali?' will start a friendly lesson. Asking someone to slow down — **अलि बिस्तारै बोल्नुहोस् न** — is never rude. Particles like **हगि** and fast forms like **गर्या** are Kathmandu youth speech; in eastern Nepal and Darjeeling you'll hear other tags and turns of phrase.

tip.title: Reacting like a Nepali
tip.body:
- Surprise: **हो र?** 'really?' · **साँच्चै भनेको?** 'seriously?' · **ला!** 'whoa!'
- Doubt: **ठट्टा गरेको?** 'are you joking?'
- Wow: **बाबै!** · **गजब!** · म त **छक्क परेँ** 'I was stunned'.
- Answer with **म सिरियस छु** 'I'm serious'.

sentences.en: Whoa, you're here too!

sentences.native: साँच्चै भनेको? तिमी बिहे गर्दै छौ?
sentences.roman: sāṃchchai bhaneko? timi bihe gardai chhau?
sentences.en: Are you serious? You're getting married?

sentences.native: ठट्टा नगर न, म सिरियस छु।
sentences.roman: ṭhaṭṭā nagara na, ma siriyas chhu.
sentences.en: Stop joking — I'm serious.
Amazing! We won.

sentences.native: उसको नेपाली सुनेर म त छक्क परेँ।
sentences.roman: usko nepāli sunera ma ta chhakka pareṃ.
sentences.en: I was stunned when I heard his Nepali.
Wow, what a crowd!

sentences.native: ठट्टा गरेको? एक कप चियाको दुई सय?
sentences.roman: ṭhaṭṭā gareko? ek kap chiyāko dui saya?
sentences.en: Are you kidding? Two hundred for a cup of tea?

sentences.native: गजब छ यो ठाउँ, फेरि आउनुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: gajab chha yo ṭhāuṃ, pheri āunuparchha.
sentences.en: This place is amazing — we have to come back.

sentences.native: ऊ कहिल्यै सिरियस हुँदैन, सधैँ ठट्टा गर्छ।
sentences.roman: u kahilyai siriyas hundaina, sadhaiṃ ṭhaṭṭā garchha.
sentences.en: He's never serious — he's always joking.

tip.title: त, नै, पो, न
tip.body:
- **त** contrast: म **त** जान्छु 'well, *I'm* going'; after a command 'just': हेर **त**.
- **नै** 'exactly, itself': आज **नै**; कोही **नै** आएन 'nobody at all'.
- **पो** 'actually (not what you thought)': यो **पो**! · नेपाली **पो** रहेछ.
- **न** softens: बस **न**. And **-ऐ**: आजै, अहिल्यै, घरमै.

sentences.native: म त जान्छु, तिमी आउने भए आऊ।
sentences.roman: ma ta jānchhu, timi āune bhae āu.
sentences.en: Well, I'm going — come if you're coming.
Just look, how lovely!
Please send it today itself, OK?
Turns out he's actually Nepali!
Not that one — this one!
Go on, eat — it's getting cold.
Damn! I left the keys at home.
Yuck, this milk has gone off.

sentences.native: म त्यही त भन्दै छु, तिमी सुन्दैनौ!
sentences.roman: ma tyahi ta bhandai chhu, timi sundainau!
sentences.en: That's exactly what I'm saying — you don't listen!

sentences.native: मलाई त थाहै थिएन, कसैले भनेन।
sentences.roman: malāi ta thāhai thiena, kasaile bhanena.
sentences.en: I had no idea — nobody told me.

tip.title: Tag questions
tip.body:
- **है?** 'OK? isn't it?' · **होइन?** 'right?' · **हगि?** (casual) 'right?'
- **नि** 'you know / and you?': तिमी **नि**?
- **र?** surprise or doubt: ऊ आयो **र**? · मलाई के थाहा **र**?
- **कि?** tentative: आउँछौ **कि**? 'coming too, maybe?'

sentences.en: This food is great, right?
You're coming too, aren't you?
Come at seven tomorrow, OK?
Did he really come?

sentences.native: मलाई के थाहा र? मैले केही देखिनँ।
sentences.roman: malāi ke thāhā ra? maile kehi dekhinaṃ.
sentences.en: How would I know? I didn't see anything.

sentences.native: म त ठीक छु, तिमी नि?
sentences.roman: ma ta ṭhik chhu, timi ni?
sentences.en: I'm fine — and you?
Would you like to come with us, maybe?

sentences.native: हुन त हो, तर अलि महँगो छ, हगि?
sentences.roman: hun ta ho, tara ali mahaṃgo chha, hagi?
sentences.en: That's true, but it's a bit expensive, isn't it?
OK, see you tomorrow then.

tip.title: Pardon? What does it mean?
tip.body:
- Didn't hear: **हजुर?** (polite) · के? (friends).
- Again, please: **दोहोर्‍याइदिनुहोस् न** · Slower: **अलि बिस्तारै** बोल्नुहोस् न.
- What does X mean? **X भनेको के हो?** / X को **अर्थ** के हो?
- For example: **उदाहरणको लागि**.

sentences.en: What does "bhyāunu" mean?
How do you pronounce this word?
Is my pronunciation OK?
What would that be in English?

sentences.native: उदाहरणको लागि, "चिया-सिया" भनेको चिया र अरू केही।
sentences.roman: udāharanko lāgi, "chiyā-siyā" bhaneko chiyā ra aru kehi.
sentences.en: For example, "chiyā-siyā" means tea and something else.

sentences.native: माफ गर्नुहोस्, मैले बुझिनँ, एक पटक दोहोर्‍याउनुहुन्छ?
sentences.roman: māph garnuhos, maile bujhinaṃ, ek paṭak dohoryāunuhunchha?
sentences.en: Sorry, I didn't understand — could you repeat that?

sentences.native: यो शब्द मैले पहिले कहिल्यै सुनेको थिइनँ।
sentences.roman: yo sabda maile pahile kahilyai suneko thiinaṃ.
sentences.en: I'd never heard this word before.

sentences.native: अलि बिस्तारै बोल्नुहोस् न, म सिक्दै छु।
sentences.roman: ali bistārai bolnuhos na, ma sikdai chhu.
sentences.en: Could you speak a bit more slowly? I'm still learning.

tip.title: Mixing in English
tip.body:
- English word + Nepali verb: **लेट भयो**, **लेट गर्नु**, **सिरियस हुनु**, **सेटिङ मिलाउनु**.
- The Nepali verb does all the grammar: लेट **गरेको**? · लेट **हुँदैन**.
- **खास** 'special': **खास केही छैन** 'nothing much'.
- Fast speech: के **गर्या**? = के गरेको?

sentences.en: Sorry, I'm a bit late.
Why are you so late?

sentences.native: टिकटको सेटिङ म मिलाउँछु, चिन्ता नगर।
sentences.roman: ṭikaṭko seṭiṅ ma milāunchhu, chintā nagara.
sentences.en: I'll sort out the tickets, don't worry.

sentences.native: खास केही होइन, खाली फोन गरेको।
sentences.roman: khās kehi hoina, khāli phon gareko.
sentences.en: Nothing special — just calling.
What a weird guy!

sentences.native: मेरो मतलब त्यो होइन, नरिसाऊ न।
sentences.roman: mero matlab tyo hoina, narisāu na.
sentences.en: That's not what I meant — don't be cross.

sentences.native: लौ न, अब जाऔँ, लेट भइसक्यो।
sentences.roman: lau na, aba jāauṃ, leṭ bhaisakyo.
sentences.en: Come on, let's go now — it's already late.
The food here isn't particularly good.

tip.title: चिया-सिया: X and stuff
tip.body:
- Repeat the word with **स-** in place of the first sound: **चिया-सिया** 'tea and stuff', **काम-साम**, **फोन-सोन**.
- It sounds casual and friendly — for friends and family.
- Fixed pair words are fine anywhere: **गफगाफ**, **लुगाफाटो**, **भाँडाकुँडा**.

sentences.native: बेलुका आऊ, चिया-सिया खाएर गफगाफ गरौँला।
sentences.roman: belukā āu, chiyā-siyā khāera gaphgāph garauṃlā.
sentences.en: Come round this evening — we'll have some tea and a chat.

sentences.native: काम-साम सकियो कि अझै अफिसमै छौ?
sentences.roman: kām-sām sakiyo ki ajhai aphismai chhau?
sentences.en: Done with work and all that, or are you still at the office?
Put your books and stuff in the bag.

sentences.native: उसले फोन-सोन केही गरेन, सिधै आयो।
sentences.roman: usle phon-son kehi garena, sidhai āyo.
sentences.en: He didn't call or anything — he just turned up.
The clothes need washing and drying on the roof.
Who's doing the dishes today?

sentences.native: हिजो राति धेरै गफगाफ भयो, सुत्न ढिलो भयो।
sentences.roman: hijo rāti dherai gaphgāph bhayo, sutna ḍhilo bhayo.
sentences.en: We chatted a lot last night, so I went to bed late.
